Hi Sarah,

Thanks for taking time today — great to learn more about Acme's ingestion pipeline and the data residency requirements for your EU customers.

Quick recap and next steps from our call:
- Redwood will provide our current subprocessor list and the SOC 2 Type II report. I've attached the most recent subprocessor export and our SOC 2 summary.
- Please confirm whether your security team needs evidence beyond the SOC 2 (e.g., architecture diagrams, encryption key custody docs) or a vendor questionnaire.
- If yes, we can have our security engineer join the thread to kick off the vendor security questionnaire and answer any technical questions.

Can you share the contact for the person who will own vendor intake (procurement or infosec)? Also, could you confirm whether Acme considers cloud providers (AWS/GCP) in-scope or expects us to list downstream subprocessors that handle customer data?

Thanks,

Marissa

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the materials and the clear recap — very helpful. I've looped in procurement (procurement@acmecorp.com) and our security lead, Tom Liang, who will own the vendor questionnaire.

Attached is our initial checklist request — for now we need:
1) Full list of subprocessors that process customer content
2) Clarification on whether Redwood's cache/backups include customer PII
3) Confirmation that Redwood uses customer-managed KMS for Private deployments

For the subprocessor question on cloud providers: we treat cloud providers (AWS) as upstream infrastructure (in-scope) and also require downstream subprocessors where Redwood engages additional vendors to process customer content (e.g., logging providers). Please include both.

I'll review the SOC 2 and get back with any follow-up questions. Who should Tom expect as the primary security contact on your side?

Best,
Sarah

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Subprocessor list & SOC 2 scope — questionnaire kickoff

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks for the checklist and for looping me in. Quick answers up front:
- Cloud providers (AWS) are listed as infrastructure subprocessors and are included in the attached export.
- Backups/caches: customer content may be temporarily cached in memory for inference; we have TTLs and KV cache controls. Backups containing customer content are not performed in hosted mode unless explicitly enabled by the customer; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed backups.
- KMS: For Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys. For Hosted we use a cloud KMS with strict access controls; we can provide key access diagrams on request.

I'll go through the checklist and provide more detailed answers and screenshots where helpful. When is a good time for a 30-minute call with your security team this week (US time)?

Regards,
Dev Patel
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
